title: Lula Seeks Fourth Term Amid Voter Fatigue
seoTitle: Lula seeks fourth term amid voter fatigue
subtitle: The former president confronts voter fatigue in the 2026 race
excerpt: Lula, 80, returns to the presidential race in 2026, seeking a fourth term after 44 years in electoral politics.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Lula, 80, returns to the presidential race in 2026, seeking a fourth term after 44 years in electoral politics. His campaign faces voter fatigue and competition from Flávio Bolsonaro, as it tries to convince the public to trust in the continuity of proposed changes.

Lula Faces Image Fatigue in 2026 Race

President Lula (PT) embarks on his seventh, and likely final, presidential bid this Sunday (4) in 2026. The main challenge is to convince voters to grant him another vote of confidence, fueling the desire for continuity with promises of change.

What Changes in Your Wallet When the Election Arrives

  • Lula highlights that change has direction, emphasizing that "we've already seen what happens when we change backward."
  • The campaign seeks to increase voter rejection of Flávio Bolsonaro, the eldest son of former president Jair Bolsonaro.
  • A Datafolha poll shows the two candidates in a technical tie: 45% of voting intentions for Lula and 42% for Flávio Bolsonaro.

What Changes in Your Wallet When the Campaign Kicks Off

  • Lula and his team are exploring the Dark Horse case, in which Flávio Bolsonaro was caught asking for money from the former owner of Banco Master, Daniel Vorcaro.
  • Speculations linking the PL candidate to militias in Rio de Janeiro were disseminated by Lula's supporters, seeking to tarnish Flávio's image.
  • Flávio's closeness to US President Donald Trump was cited as a risk of foreign interference in the election.

What Changes in Your Wallet as the First Round Approaches

Despite the efforts, Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro conclude the first round with high levels of voting intention, around 45% for Lula and 42% for Flávio, according to Datafolha. The margin of error is two percentage points, plus or minus.

What Changes in Your Wallet as the Campaign Intensifies

Lula's campaign began with lighter-toned advertisements, attempting to improve government approval. Subsequently, it shifted focus to criticizing his opponent, seeking to increase voter rejection of the PL candidate.

What Changes in Your Wallet When the Election Ends

With the dispute still open, Lula continues to emphasize the need for continuity in changes, while Flávio Bolsonaro tries to present himself as a fresh face on the national scene. The final outcome will depend on the debate surrounding voter fatigue and each candidate's ability to convince the electorate that change can continue towards the future.

With information from G1, Folha de S.Paulo, Brasil 247.
